SearchSearchFacebookTwitterEmailSMSBlue SkyWhatsappPrintRedditFlipboardPinterestLinkedinLatest StoriesPoliticsU.S. NewsWorldSportsBusinessHealthSelectedTiplineIsraelIsrael’s Eisenkot condemns arson attacks by Jewish settlers in West BankEisenkot called the attacks “Jewish terrorism,” saying that “extremist groups that set fire to ​vehicles and homes are undermining regional stability, putting lives at risk and doing grave damage to Israel’s national security.”Listen to this article with a free profile00:0000:00Palestinian men inspect burnt-out and destroyed vehicles following a reported arson attack by Israeli settlers in Kafr Malik in the Israeli-occupied West Bank on Nov. 22.Zain Jaafar / AFP via GettyShareAdd NBC News to GoogleNov. 22, 2026, 9:17 AM EST / Source: ReutersBy ReutersRAMALLAH, West Bank — Israeli militant settlers attacked Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank early on ​Sunday, starting fires and scrawling racist graffiti, residents said, prompting an accusation of “Jewish terrorism” from the ‌man trying to form an Israeli government.

The attacks, the latest in an escalation that began after Hamas launched attacks on Israel from the Gaza Strip in 2023, come nearly a month after an inconclusive election stripped incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his majority. Opposition ​leader Gadi Eisenkot has been asked to form a government, though his prospects seem little better.

Reuters saw burned-out ​Palestinian vehicles and walls spray-painted with slogans such as “Revenge” in villages near Ramallah. No one immediately ⁠claimed responsibility and no injuries were reported.

Eisenkot called the attacks “Jewish terrorism,” saying that “extremist groups that set fire to ​vehicles and homes are undermining regional stability, putting lives at risk and doing grave damage to Israel’s national security and ​foreign relations.”

He said the policies of Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, ultranationalist ministers in Netanyahu’s Cabinet, had “brought the area to the brink of anarchy, and the authorities have yet to address the crisis.”

United Nations bodies and most countries of the world deny ​the legality of the settlements, which make the prospect of an independent Palestinian state ever more remote, a position ​Israel disputes.

A Palestinian man inspects damaged cars following an attack reportedly carried out by Israeli settlers in Deir Abu Mashaal, west of the city of Ramallah, on Nov. 22.Zain Jaafar / AFP via GettyIsraeli police said they had opened an investigation into the attacks, while the military condemned the violence, saying soldiers and police ‌had ⁠been dispatched to the areas of Deir as-Sudan, Deir Abu Masha’al, Kafr Malik and At-Tuwani “following reports and footage showing vehicles being set on fire and graffiti being sprayed in the area.”

Ben-Gvir replied in an X post that Eisenkot’s condemnation amounted to selling out to Arab parties, which could be part of a possible new government. Smotrich favors settlement expansion and ​wants Israel to annex the ​West Bank.

Israel’s parliament was sworn in ​on Nov. 10 ⁠without a new government, after the election on Oct. 27 stripped Netanyahu of his majority but left others with no clear path to power.

President Isaac Herzog has tasked Eisenkot, who heads the center-right Yashar party, with forming a government, while Netanyahu remains ⁠caretaker prime ​minister.

Unless Eisenkot forms a unity government with Netanyahu, he is likely ​to need support from Arab parties to be able to count on a majority of the parliament’s 120 seats.

If no one is able to form a ​government, another election will be held next year.
